## 13. Risk and control self-assessment

The RCSA is the primary mechanism through which the first line discharges its ownership ofrisk. It is a structured assessment,performedby the people whooperate the process,ofwhatcouldgo wrong,whatcontrols exist,and howwell those controls work.

13.1Scope and frequency

| SCOPE UNIT | FULLASSESSMENT | REFRESH | TRIGGERFOROUT-OF-CYCLEASSESSMENT |
|---|---|---|---|
| Material business processes | Annual | Semi-annual | Material change to the process,system or organisation |
| Important business services | Annual | Quarterly | Anybreachofimpact tolerance |
| Legal entities | Annual | Annual | Change in regulatory permissions or licence conditions |
| Criticalthirdparties | Annual | Semi-annual | Change in service scope,sub-contracting or adverse assessment outcome |

## 13.2Requiredsteps

1. Define the scope — the process, service or entity assessed, with clear boundaries and hand-off points.

2.Identifyrisks—whatcould prevent theobjectives ofthatscope from being met,classified to the taxonomy.

a inherent risk — impact and likelihood before controls, using the Appendix A scales.

4. identify controls — the specific controls addressing each risk, distinguishing key from supporting controls.

5. Assess control effectiveness — design and operation, supported by testing evidence.

6. Rate residualrisk—the exposure remaining, justifiedby the control assessment.

7.Compare to appetite—and determine whether treatment or acceptance is required.

8. Raise issues — for every control rated partially effective or ineffective.

9.Attest—formal sign-off by the accountable executive.

10. Second-line challenge — independent review and recorded challenge by the Group Risk function.
